subject: Edge cache invalidations and SLA offset appeal
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: ops@greylabs.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Edge cache invalidations and SLA offset appeal

Hi GreyLabs ops team,

Quick note following our SRE dashboards: on 2026-11-29 between 23:40 and 01:10 UTC we saw a sustained latency spike and elevated 5xx rate affecting a subset of your edge POPs that serve our account. Traffic path traces indicate repeated cache invalidations originating from your control plane that coincided with an origin TLS handshake failure. Impact summary attached.

We consider ~1h30m of partial degradation (significant tail latency and increased errors) that overlapped our peak for that region. We understand some invalidations are routine, but this appears to have been triggered by an upstream event and then amplified by aggressive invalidation churn.

Request: please provide your incident timeline and formal justification for treating this as a third-party maintenance exclusion or, if not applicable, confirm the SLA credit calculation you will apply. I attached:
- edge_invalidation_log.csv (filtered keys/events)
- latency_metrics_20261129-30.pdf (token-level latency by route)

We'd like a written response by EOD GMT+0 on 2026-12-03 so we can present to GreyLabs legal and our CS team.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

Redwood Inference

---
Note: forwarding to Marissa for commercial alignment and next steps on credits.
From: ops@greylabs.com <ops@greylabs.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Edge cache invalidations and SLA offset appeal

Evelyn / Marissa,

Thanks for the heads up and the logs. We investigated and the cache invalidations you observed were initiated by our automated certificate rotation handler at 03:07 UTC on 2026-11-29, which forced a series of origin revalidations and subsequent CDN propagation events. We recorded an elevated invalidation rate for ~22 minutes across three POPs.

We have an internal incident file (ops_incident_9876.txt) attached that contains our trigger events and the upstream CA rotation notice. Per our SLA Section 4.2, events caused by third-party CA rotations that force control-plane invalidations are treated as exclusions when the activity originates from a mandatory trust update at the CA.

That said, we agree there was some residual propagation after the initial activity window; we are compiling a timeline and will propose a credit for the residual impact. Expect our formal timeline and proposed credit by 2026-12-07.

Best,
GreyLabs Ops (on behalf of EdgeCDN)
ops@greylabs.com

Attachment: ops_incident_9876.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ops@greylabs.com
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Edge cache invalidations and SLA offset appeal

Hi — appreciate the quick triage. A couple of commercial points to keep on the table:

- From GreyLabs' perspective, our customers expect us to meet latency SLOs regardless of whether the root cause originates in a CA rotation. If an automated third-party action results in control-plane invalidations that materially affect our provisioned performance, we treat that as an operational impact requiring remediation or credit.
- We're open to reasonable exclusions for the narrow window you described (22 minutes), but our internal telemetry shows degraded tails and elevated error rate for ~1 hour 8 minutes beyond that, primarily because invalidation churn retriggered several origin calls.

Requested next steps:
1) Provide a detailed minute-by-minute timeline for 2026-11-29 02:45–04:30 UTC including: invalidation API calls, control-plane events, and any changes to TTLs you propagated.
2) Confirm whether this was an automated CA/PKI push you performed, or a mandatory external rotation you consumed.
3) If the exclusion applies only to the CA rotation window, propose a credit calculation for the remaining 1h8m of measurable impact.

For reference, here's our SLA clause that we're using for interpretation: https://redwood.example.com/sla-clauses#maintenance. We're preparing a short mutual action plan to keep this from recurring — attached (mutual_action_plan.docx). If we cannot agree on the credit, we'll escalate to legal for an interpretation of the exclusion language.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0199
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: ops@greylabs.com
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Edge cache invalidations and SLA offset appeal

Ops — thanks for the incident file. I'm an SRE on the Redwood account and pulled traces from our side; summarizing technical findings below.

On Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 11:45 AM ops@greylabs.com wrote:
> We investigated and the cache invalidations you observed were initiated by our automated certificate rotation handler at 03:07 UTC on 2026-11-29...

Our analysis: your ops file matches the initial activity at ~03:07 UTC. That initial burst aligns with the 22-minute invalidation window you described (03:07–03:29 UTC). However, our request traces show a second phase of revalidation churn from 03:40–04:48 UTC affecting ~37% of routed hosts for Redwood customers. The root cause for the second phase is: when origin TLS handshakes began failing (due to the rotation), our clients retried with different origin endpoints; those retries caused cache keys to miss and regenerated mitigate calls to the control plane which then triggered further invalidations in a feedback loop.

Key points:
- Initial invalidation window: 03:07–03:29 UTC (we accept this as the CA-triggered activity).
- Residual propagation and churn: 03:40–04:48 UTC (this is where we request credit).
- The residual period maps to 1h8m of elevated tail latency and higher error rate in two of our busiest routes.

We propose the following, aiming to resolve without legal escalation:
1) GreyLabs acknowledges the 03:07–03:29 UTC window as CA-triggered exclusion.
2) GreyLabs provides a credit for the residual 03:40–04:48 UTC window equal to 35% of the per-minute consumed tokens for that period (proposed_credit_calc.csv attached). We are open to negotiating the percentage; our figure reflects the portion of requests that experienced protocol-level retries and cache-miss amplification.
3) Execute the mutual action plan in mutual_action_plan.docx (we'll sign and return).
4) Sign the SLA offset agreement via DocuSign: https://secure.docusign.com/Redwood-GreyLabs-SLA-offset-4721

Please respond with confirmation of the exclusion window and whether you accept the residual credit calculation or want to counter. If you need an on-call SRE call to walk the traces together, we can set one up for tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
